scope: Ten nonclinical imaging foundations, two per stage from preschool to undergraduate. These lessons teach observation, representation, measurement and reconstruction; they do not teach children to diagnose, select examinations, operate scanners or report clinical findings.
bridge_assumptions: Stages 0–1 use ordinary toys, drawings and adult-supported exploration. No medical images, radiation devices, cutting activities or diagnosis tasks are required.
Age bands follow the existing Primer stages: 3–5, 6–9, 10–13, 14–17, undergraduate. Master’s-level radiology remains in the existing specialist library.
All stage-0 nodes have no prerequisites. Later links form a directed acyclic graph and refer to existing math and physics lessons where quantitative grounding is needed.
Paper layers, block grids, rope waves and other catalog objects are explicitly limited analogies. model_context records where a shared interactive object does not simulate the imaging mechanism.
Transmission and echo arithmetic use invented or idealized nonclinical examples. Medical-method descriptions explain signals without advice about patient imaging.
These nodes must bypass clinical reference attachment and reporting-template validation. Keep the existing clinical nodes unchanged.

sources.title: NIBIB — Computed Tomography (CT)
sources.supports: CT reconstructs cross-sectional images from X-ray measurements; stacked slices can represent a volume.

sources.title: NIBIB — Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
sources.supports: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radiofrequency excitation/detection rather than ionizing X-rays.

sources.title: NIBIB — Ultrasound
sources.supports: Ultrasound imaging measures returned high-frequency sound signals.
